ai.description: This small frog (20–25 mm) is typically yellowish-brown with a distinct dark interorbital bar and a pale belly. It features a pointed snout and granular skin on the dorsum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes andersoni* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or orange vocal sac and the presence of a prominent, dark-edged white spot on the groin.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes andersoni* inhabits evergreen forests and tea plantations in the Eastern Himalayas and Northeast India, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Anderson's Bubble-nest Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden among vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes andersoni* undergoes direct development within terrestrial foam nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically producing small clutches of eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes andersoni* is found in Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Nagaland) at elevations ranging from 200 to 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes andersoni* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps heard primarily in moist, forested shrub habitats.
